#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script converted from Slurm
# Note: Flux does not support in-script directives for resource specification
# This script should be submitted with the following command:
# flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -t 4d --setattr=system.memory-per-cpu=8000M --job-name=Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base --output=Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base.out.txt --error=Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base.err.txt script.sh
#
# Resource specifications:
# -N 1         : 1 node (implicit from original Slurm script with ntasks=1)
# -n 1         : 1 task (from --ntasks=1)
# -t 4d        : 4 day walltime (from --time=4-0:00)
# --setattr=system.memory-per-cpu=8000M : 8000 MB memory per CPU (from --mem-per-cpu=8000)
# --job-name=  : job name (from -J Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base)
# --output=    : stdout redirection (from -o Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base.out.txt)
# --error=     : stderr redirection (from -e Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base.err.txt)
#
# Note: Flux uses 'd' suffix for days in time specification
# Note: Memory specification syntax may vary by Flux version
# Alternative memory syntax: --setattr=system.memory=8000M (if only 1 CPU is allocated)

# Original job name: Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base
# Set at submission: flux batch --job-name=Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base ...

# Original output/error files:
# Set at submission with full filenames

# Partition: mono
# Note: Flux does not have partitions in the same way as Slurm
# Queue selection is handled through Flux's scheduling configuration
# Performance impact: Job scheduling depends on site-specific Flux queue policies
# Consult site documentation for equivalent resource pools or queues

# Memory per CPU: 8000 MB
# Note: Memory requests in Flux use --setattr=system.memory-per-cpu syntax
# or --setattr=system.memory for total memory
# Performance impact: Without explicit memory request, job gets default allocation
# which may be insufficient and cause OOM errors
# The exact attribute name may vary by Flux version - verify with local documentation

source /etc/profile.modules

module load gcc
module load matlab

cd ~/deepLearn

# Original: srun ./deepFunction ...
# Note: In Flux batch context, use 'flux run' instead of 'srun' for launching tasks
# For single-task jobs, direct execution is also acceptable
# Using flux run for consistency with Flux task launching
flux run -n 1 ./deepFunction 4 'RBM' 'DBN' '128  1500  1000    10' '0  0  0  0' '4_dec_real' 'PERS_base' "'iteration.n_epochs', 'learning.lrate', 'learning.cd_k', 'learning.persistent_cd', 'parallel_tempering.use'" '200 1e-3 1 1 0' "'iteration.n_epochs', 'learning.persistent_cd'" '200 0'

# Alternative: Direct execution without flux run for single task
# ./deepFunction 4 'RBM' 'DBN' '128  1500  1000    10' '0  0  0  0' '4_dec_real' 'PERS_base' "'iteration.n_epochs', 'learning.lrate', 'learning.cd_k', 'learning.persistent_cd', 'parallel_tempering.use'" '200 1e-3 1 1 0' "'iteration.n_epochs', 'learning.persistent_cd'" '200 0'

issues: The script correctly documents that Flux does not support in-script resource directives and provides proper submission command syntax in comments.

The memory attribute syntax '--setattr=system.memory-per-cpu=8000M' may not be valid in all Flux versions. The standard Flux attribute for memory is typically '--setattr=system.memory' for total memory. The 'memory-per-cpu' attribute may not be recognized. Verify with 'flux batch --help' or local Flux documentation.
The recommended submission command is very long. Consider breaking it into multiple lines with backslashes for readability, or using environment variables.
The time specification '-t 4d' (4 days) is correct Flux syntax, but very long runtimes may be subject to site-specific policies or limits. Verify that 4-day jobs are permitted on your Flux instance.

The script uses 'flux run -n 1' to launch a single task, which is appropriate. However, for a single-task job within a batch script that already allocated 1 task (-n 1 at submission), direct execution without 'flux run' would also work and be simpler.
The memory specification of 8000M (8GB) per CPU should be verified against the actual memory requirements of the MATLAB deepFunction program to avoid OOM errors or resource waste.

Consider using the simpler memory syntax in the submission command: '--setattr=system.memory=8000M' or '--setattr=system.memory=8G' instead of memory-per-cpu, since only 1 CPU/task is being requested.

The output/error file paths are relative (Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base.out.txt). Ensure the submission directory is the intended location for these files, or use absolute paths in the submission command.

No cores-per-task specification is provided. The default is typically 1 core per task. If the MATLAB code uses threading or parallel toolbox features, consider adding '-c <cores>' to the submission command.

The job name 'Deep-RBM_DBN_4_dec_real_PERS_base' contains underscores and is quite long (35 characters). While generally acceptable, verify there are no character limits or restrictions in your Flux configuration.

source /etc/profile.modules

module load gcc
module load matlab
cd ~/deepLearn && srun ./deepFunction 4 'RBM' 'DBN' '128  1500  1000    10' '0  0  0  0' '4_dec_real' 'PERS_base' "'iteration.n_epochs', 'learning.lrate', 'learning.cd_k', 'learning.persistent_cd', 'parallel_tempering.use'" '200 1e-3 1 1 0' "'iteration.n_epochs', 'learning.persistent_cd'" '200 0'
